link.per: one percentage-point increase in TSP concentration relative to place start; local linear elasticity approximation near start
link.group: infant birth cohorts exposed to TSP; internal-cause deaths per live births
link.anchor: IV elasticity 0.45; reported design/subsample elasticity spread 0.3 to 0.7. Per pct-of-start point divide each elasticity by 100.
link.source: Chay and Greenstone 2003, Air Quality, Infant Mortality, and the Clean Air Act of 1970, NBER w10053, pp.20-21,26-27; https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w10053/w10053.pdf

research.result: Page 26: inverse-sampling-error-weighted IV elasticity 0.45. Pages 20 to 21 report 0.3 to 0.6; page 27 reports 0.6 to 0.7 near the regulatory cutoff.
research.breadth: US monitored counties, 1971 to 1972 changes induced by Clean Air Act nonattainment. TSP, not PM2.5 or an air-quality index. Outcome is internal-cause infant deaths per live births.
research.access: Working paper full text and tables read.
research.conversion: size = 0.45 / 100; range = [0.3 / 100, 0.7 / 100]. The cause is percent of starting TSP, so a one-point increase gives a 0.45% local proportional mortality increase.
research.transportLimit: Study specification/subsample spread is not a CI or modern PM2.5 coefficient. Requires TSP-specific cause and infant internal-cause outcome readers; neither was verified. No supported general air-quality-index conversion.
research.readerStatus: No person feels this yet: no cause or outcome reader was verified in this research batch. A numeric entry is not runtime activation proof.
